label: Exploratory: same method as the presets, not checked against a national reference series.
method: Per 2-degree cell: L = Aqua daytime hotspot detections / (S-NPP detections x 2012-2020 Aqua/S-NPP ratio by calendar month), on days both satellites returned data anywhere on Earth; 95% 16-day block bootstrap (1000, seed 20261114); 2012-2020 years scored leave-one-out for the placebo range. L, its interval and the bootstrap weights are analysis/statistics/audit.py's, imported as written. Counts are every daytime detection (count_all). L above 1: Aqua counts more than the fixed clock predicts; below 1: fewer. Neither direction is attributed to orbit drift alone. lst_shift_min = Aqua's median local solar time (near-nadir detections passing the counting filters) minus the median of its 2012-2020 yearly medians, in minutes. n_aqua_2025 and n_snpp_2025 are counts on the retained days. noise_floor = largest |L - 1| over the nine placebo years; placebo_min and placebo_max = their lowest and highest L; outside_noise = L outside placebo_min to placebo_max (descriptive, not a significance test).
sources: NASA FIRMS yearly country archives (MODIS C6.1; VIIRS 375 m S-NPP and NOAA-20), https://firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov/download/ (files under https://firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov/data/country/zips/). NASA data, open use; cite as NASA FIRMS.
analysis/statistics/audit.py (this repo): L, the bootstrap and the calendar rule, used as written.

mask_rule.rule: A cell-year is too_few_fires when the fixed-clock (expected) Aqua count is under 300, or the 95% interval half-width is over 25% of L, or L or its interval is not a finite number. The first two are the preset audit's own insufficient_data rule (analysis/statistics/audit.py).
mask_rule.applies_to: status is the 2025 reading, status_2024 the 2024 reading. A masked reading carries no L, interval or outside_noise value.
mask_rule.meaning: too_few_fires means the count is too small to read. It does not mean the count agreed with the fixed clock.

retained_days_rule: A satellite counts as down on a day with no daytime detection anywhere on Earth. The preset audit uses anywhere in Brazil; the difference is measured in analysis/global/out/benchmarks.json (G1).
